# limen_role_mapping (Resource)

A Limen role mapping: which IdP groups get which roles.

Writers can never assign a built-in role (`limen:admin`, `limen:auditor`), and a mapping that widens standing access is held for approval.

Every write is checked against the document's etag and owner, so Terraform never overwrites a change it hasn't seen, and never touches a document another channel (Git, the console) or another source owns. During plan the provider dry-runs the change (`plan_checks`) and shows who gains or loses access.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Widens standing access, so a bot's write is held for a person to approve.
# The plan says so; apply names the change, or waits with approval_timeout.
resource "limen_role_mapping" "payments" {
  name = "payments-staging"

  spec = [
    { idp_group = "okta-payments-eng", roles = [limen_role.payments_read.name] },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique per kind across the control plane, and immutable: changing it replaces the document. 1 to 128 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, and `-`. A bot writer's names must match its grant's name patterns.
- `spec` (Dynamic) The mapping's `spec`: a list of `{ idp_group = "...", roles = ["..."] }`, in exactly the shape of the YAML spec. Limen parses it strictly: unknown fields are refused. `null` attributes are left out.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free text shown in the console and the CLI.
- `labels` (Map of String) Labels that roles select on. Keys are lowercase `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `-`. For a resource from a profile, only the keys and values the profile allows; its fixed labels are in `effective_labels`.
- `namespace` (String) The owner's namespace, the permission scope. Defaults to the provider's `default_namespace`, else the bot's grant's namespace. Moving a document to another namespace needs a person with `limen:admin`.
- `source` (String) The owner's source. Defaults to the provider's `default_source`. Changing it transfers the document (for example after `terraform state mv` into another state); a writer may move documents only between its own sources.

### Read-Only

- `channel` (String) How the owner writes the document: always `api` for documents Terraform manages.
- `created_at` (String) When the document was created (RFC 3339).
- `effective_labels` (Map of String) What roles select on: `labels` plus, for a resource from a profile, the profile's fixed labels.
- `effective_spec_json` (String) What enforcement uses, as JSON: for a resource from a profile, the profile's template merged with `spec`; otherwise the same as `spec`. Use `jsondecode()` to read it.
- `etag` (String) Opaque; changes whenever the document or its owner changes. Every write sends it back, so Limen refuses to overwrite a change Terraform hasn't seen.
- `id` (String) The document's name.
- `policy_version` (Number) The policy version this revision first appeared in.
- `updated_at` (String) When this revision was written (RFC 3339).
- `updated_by` (String) Who wrote this revision: a person, or `bot:<name>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import limen_role_mapping.payments payments-staging
```
